chapter: First bass jobs in California, Chicago and the move to New York
title: Going to New York with Stuff Smith, Frankie Newton and Eddie Heywood
summary: He arrived in New York in 1941 and quickly worked with Stuff Smith, Newton and Heywood.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So this leaves me hanging. Should I come back to California, 'cause I'd worked everywhere in Chicago and I was tired of these repeats. I said, shall I go to Chicago, go to California, or shall I go to New York. So I said, well, since I'm this close, the least I can do is go back to California.
I got to New York with 50 cents. I arrived in Chicago with 35 cents.
What year was this, when you first arrived in New York?
'41. So first thing off the bat, I got a job before I could deposit my transfer, with Stuff Smith. At Kelly's Stables. Then I worked with Frankie Newton.
Had you been acquainted with Smith before, or did they know you by reputation, or what?
They weren't even familiar with your playing?
No. It's just that all New Yorkers figured themselves the greatest, you know, and they had heard me jam. That's how I got the jobs. So --
Where did you jam, in New York?
Yeah, yeah. So after Stuff Smith, I found Eddie Heywood with a trio, at the Village Vanguard. He didn't have a bass player so I'd sit down there every night.
Little boy called Keg Parnell. He used to work with Benny Carter, that's the time that Eddie Heywood was with him. [PAUSE]
